title: Vanishing and finiteness for procyclic cohomology
statement: Let ell be prime and A a finite ring killed by ell^s. For every discrete continuous A-module M for the additive ell-adic integers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], H^q(M) is zero for q>1; if M is finite, H^0(M) and H^1(M) are finite. Cohomology is [def-exc-continuous-cohomology].

proof.text: Apply the two-term computation. Above degree one the term of the complex is zero, so the complex is exact at that degree and its homology is zero. If M is finite, the two terms in degrees zero and one are finite by the given linear equivalences. Each homology is a quotient of the kernel of the next differential, a submodule of a finite term, so it is finite. Transfer both conclusions through the computation isomorphisms.

theorem procyclic_cohomology_conclusions
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (s : ℕ) (A : Type v) [Ring A] [Finite A]
    (hA : (l ^ s : ℕ) • (1 : A) = 0)
    (M : DiscreteContinuousRep.{v, 0, w} A (Multiplicative ℤ_[l])) :
    (∀ q : ℕ, 1 < q →
      IsZero ((discreteContinuousCohomologyFunctor.{0,v,w}
        (Multiplicative ℤ_[l]) A q).obj M)) ∧
      (Finite M.obj.V →
        Finite (((discreteContinuousCohomologyFunctor.{0,v,w}
          (Multiplicative ℤ_[l]) A 0).obj M).carrier) ∧
        Finite (((discreteContinuousCohomologyFunctor.{0,v,w}
          (Multiplicative ℤ_[l]) A 1).obj M).carrier))
